content.text:
I compared the r1 frames with the r0 frames and with my prediction, by eye only. I wrote a small pixel-measurement script to back this up, but running it needed your approval and wasn't granted, so there are no numbers here.

| Frame | My prediction | r1 | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | Unchanged: cold pit, no smoke | Identical to r0: cold pit, no flame, no smoke. | Matches. |
| 25 | A hint of haze above the flame tip, almost invisible against the flame's glow | No smoke I can pick out at all; only the flame's halo and a few sparks. | Matches, at the fainter end. |
| 55 | Thin, see-through grey wisps; no white core over the flame | One faint grey wisp up and to the left of the flames, see-through, lighter than the grass. The near-white strands from r0 are gone. | Matches. |
| 100 | Same column shape and height, as soft see-through grey haze | The base, about 0.5–0.8 m over the pit, is a soft grey haze, clearly lighter than the grass and no longer a lit cloud. Above it there's only one barely visible puff, about level with the standing camper's waist. In r0 the column showed clearly up to there. | **Partly.** The base matches; the height doesn't. The column now reads about half as tall. |
| 110 | Still a cloud low at the pit, as grey haze, not a bright white mass | Dimmer than r0's near-white mass, but still the brightest and most solid smoke in the strip: a pale grey cloud about 1.3 m across, low over the pit, with small flames still burning. | **Partly.** It's dimmer, but it still reads as a cloud more than a haze. |
| 160 | The last puffs barely visible; they might disappear entirely | One very faint puff low over the pit, behind the thought bubble's tail. | Matches: barely visible, but not gone. |

## Explaining the two misses

**Frame 100, the shorter column.** I was wrong to predict the same height. Lowering the peak alpha lowers the whole fade-out with it, because alpha falls in a straight line from the 15% stop to 0 at the end of life. So a puff 60% through its life, roughly 1–1.5 m up, has about half the alpha it had in r0. That was already faint at the top in r0, and now it falls below what shows against the dark grass. Nothing about the height changed; the top half is just invisible. The intent asks for about 2 m, so r1 is now short of the intent at the top, where r0 overshot at the bottom.

**Frame 110, the cloud.** The same shift happens in r0 and r1, so it doesn't come from the alpha:
- **The douse takes 0.5 s.** At frame 110 the fire is still at about 0.2, so it's still emitting, and every puff from the last second is at its brightest, low over the pit.
- **The background got darker.** The flames and their light are shrinking, so the bright flame no longer hides the smoke above it, and the firelit ground behind it is darker.

In frame 100, the same smoke sits partly inside the flame's glow and reads as less. In frame 110 the haze has dark ground behind it, so it stands out as a cloud.

## Overall

The change did what was aimed at: the glowing, near-white core from frames 55–110 is gone, and the smoke now reads as grey haze. The cost is the column's top half, which you can no longer see. That's the gap from the intent I'd look at next, with a change to the shape of the alpha fade, not its peak. I haven't edited anything.

status_detail: r1 vs prediction: core gone, column top now too faint
